title: sre weekly ops sync notes - 2026-03-16 (draft)
body:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review
Date: 2026-03-16 (Tuesday) - 10:00am PT
Owner: Jordan Lee (notes)
Attendees: Priya, Marcus, Samira (partial), on-call rotation
Status: Draft prep notes / agenda + follow-ups

Goals for this meeting:
- Quick health check: SLO burn, error budget consumption, paging trends
- Review top incidents since last sync and stabilization status
- Discuss recurring noise sources and mitigation roadmap
- Action items and owners for the week

Agenda (20-30m):
1) Quick metrics snapshot (5m)
   - Request rate: ~520 req/s (7d avg)
   - 95p latency: 220ms (up 12% week-over-week)
   - Error rate (4xx/5xx): 0.55% (0.4% last week)
   - SLOs: availability (99.95% monthly target) — current month to date: 99.87% -> 0.08% burn of error budget
   - P95 tail on form-fill route is main contributor to latency bump

2) Paging trends (5m)
   - Pages per week: avg 6 -> last 7 days: 11 (spike due to incident A & noisy alert)
   - Top pagers: high GC pause on cache node pool (incident A), API gateway timeouts (incident B)
   - On-call load: Priya had 3 pages over weekend, all resolved within target MTTR but follow-ups needed

3) Incidents (10m)
   - Incident A (2026-03-14) - cache node GC causing KV cache invalidations -> increased latencies and 5xx on a subset of requests
     * Status: mitigated (forced restart + GC flags applied), RCA in progress
     * Short-term: pin GC flags on affected nodes; add proactive mem pressure alert to SRE playbook
     * Long-term: move cache nodes to larger instance class or tune heap sizing; track in backlog SRE-1823
   - Incident B (2026-03-12) - API gateway timeouts during region failover test
     * Status: resolved; root cause: circuit-breaker misconfiguration + insufficient retry policy for new client SDKs
     * Remediation: update gateway retry policy; notify client SDK owners (ping in #dev-apis)
     * Follow-up: add canary test for gateway changes + runbook step for rollback
   - Incident C (2026-03-10) - noisy downstream model endpoint (reduced throughput) -> failover didn't trigger reliably
     * Status: closed with postmortem draft; action: extend detection window and lower threshold for failover trigger

4) Runbook & alerts hygiene (3m)
   - Alerts reviewed: reduce noise by consolidating duplicate alarms for same underlying symptom
   - Proposed: suppress low-signal alerts on staging namespaces; add alert annotation to link to runbook PR

5) Open discussion / blockers (2m)
   - Prioritization of cache-sizing vs gateway retry changes (we have limited eng cycles this sprint)
   - Request from product: lower P95 on form-fill by 30% for upcoming feature launch (needs capacity plan)

Action items (owner - due):
- Jordan: Finish incident A RCA draft + upload to Confluence (due 2026-03-18)
- Priya: Add proactive mem-pressure alert and test in staging (due 2026-03-19)
- Marcus: Gateways - update retry policy & add canary test; coordinate with dev-apis (due 2026-03-22)
- Samira: Capacity plan proposal for cache node sizing options and cost estimate (due 2026-03-23)
- On-call rotation: include step to validate failover trigger in weekly checklist (owner: rotation lead) (due 2026-03-20)
- Ops docs: consolidate duplicate alerts + annotate runbooks with alert IDs (owner: Jordan/Marcus) (due 2026-03-24)

Notes to self / talking points:
- Emphasize that pages are resolvable quickly but frequency rising -> signal that we need permanent fixes not just band-aids
- For incident A, highlight that restarts reduced impact but didn't prevent recurrence; avoid promising immediate infra spend without cost tradeoff
- Ask product about ship date for form-fill feature; align cost vs SLO risk if we upgrade cache nodes

Follow-up items to track in backlog (short descriptions, will create JIRA tickets):
- SRE-1823: Cache node sizing evaluation + pilot (priority: high)
- SRE-1830: Gateway canary + rollback runbook (priority: medium)
- SRE-1831: Alert consolidation sweep (priority: low)

Prep before meeting:
- Pull up last 30 days of SLO burn graph from SRE dashboard (Jordan)
- Have incident A logs & heap dumps ready (Priya)
- Quick cost delta calc for moving cache nodes to larger instance types (Samira)

Misc / scratchpad thoughts (informal):
- Consider temporary auto-restart policy for cache nodes hitting OOM-ish on weekends (hate to do it but could reduce pages overnight)
- If we tune GC flags, document changes and add to image bake pipeline so next node pool has it by default
- Remind dev-apis to include explicit retry/backoff guidance in SDK changelog

End of notes. Will tidy after sync and upload final to shared_drives/engineering/observability/sre-ops if agreed.
